text:
A 1947 rent law still shapes South Mumbai property.

Bloomberg reported in 2012 that a family paid about ₹1,300 a month for a 2,600 sq ft flat on Nepean Sea Road, where market rent was over ₹1 lakh. Bombay's 1947 Act froze rents at 1940 levels; research by IDFC Institute and NYU Marron (2015) found controlled rent can be one-thousandth of market rent.

Why it matters to buyers and investors: in an old tenanted building the landlord earns little and repairs stall, but the tenant's right is worth real money. That building's redevelopment paid the tenants about ₹14 crore to move. Price a cessed building by who holds the tenancy, not just the land.

Sources: Bloomberg (2012), Tandel et al. (2015). Rupee figures converted at the 2012 rate. Education only.

Who really owns the value here: the landlord or the tenant?
